questions.question: What happens when you click the "Run" button in your code editor?

options.text: The computer executes the entire program from start to finish at full speed.
The computer pauses on every single line and asks for permission.
The computer deletes all previous lines and closes the window.
The computer converts the Python code into an image file.

questions.explanation_correct:
✅ CORRECT!
The Run button instructs Python to execute all instructions sequentially from top to bottom at normal speed.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Not quite!
Run executes the script from start to finish. If you want to pause and inspect line-by-line, you use Debug and Step.

questions.question: What happens when you click on a line number in the gutter to add a Breakpoint (●)?

options.text: It marks a pause point where the debugger will temporarily stop execution.
It comments out that line so Python skips it completely.
It makes that line repeat 10 times automatically.
It encrypts the line with a password.

questions.explanation_correct:
🎯 SPOT ON!
A Breakpoint tells the debugger: 'Pause here so the programmer can look at variables and inspect memory.'
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Try Again!
Breakpoints do not delete or skip lines. They pause execution during a debug session so you can inspect state.

questions.question: How does the "Step" (⏭) button work during debugging?

options.text: It advances execution by exactly one line, allowing you to observe variable changes.
It skips all remaining code in the file.
It reverses time and un-runs the previous line.
It shuts down the computer safely.

questions.explanation_correct:
💡 NICE!
Stepping moves the program forward one line at a time, making it easy to spot where things go wrong.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Not quite!
Step executes the next single line of code so you can watch memory values change gradually.

questions.question: Where can you check the current values and types of variables while stepping through code?

options.text: The Memory & Variables Inspector table in the right panel.
The keyboard settings menu.
The browser history tab.
The operating system recycle bin.

questions.explanation_correct:
🔍 EXCELLENT!
The Memory / Variables table displays all active variables, their Python data types (e.g. str, int), and their live values.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Try Again!
The Variables Inspector table in the editor panel shows variable names, types, and values in memory.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Output Console Terminal?

options.text: To display text output printed by print() and show runtime messages or errors.
To design 3D animations automatically.
To format the computer's hard drive.
To write code on your behalf without typing.

questions.explanation_correct:
🏆 MODULE COMPLETE!
The output console is the screen where your program's text results, greetings, numbers, and error messages appear!
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Almost!
The Output Console shows what your code prints out (using print()) and reports system messages or error traces.
